text:
sofia: Heads up — after last night's routing rollout I’m seeing slowdowns on the console: sparklines + per-series widgets lagging, main-thread parse up, and LCP shifts in EU. Repro steps: open dashboard > switch to 90d > hover on series (observed on canary + prod). :eyes:
cheng: Seeing it too. Telemetry: kvcache.hit_rate dropped ~40% for heatmap/series endpoints since ~02:00 UTC. Main-thread parse time +110-140ms per page. Stack traces show more repeated JSON.parse on small chunks.
morgan: Could be cache key fragmentation. We changed prefetch.window from 50 -> 10 in the rollout and adjusted routing weights to favor the prefetched variant. If the variant injection changed request headers, keying might not match existing cache entries.
alex: Agreed. I can reproduce locally by toggling X-Route-Variant header. When header present we get different cache keys and a bunch of small bundle fetches rather than prefix hits.
sofia: Quick checks — any recent bundle splits that would increase small-file count?
liz: No heavy bundle churn in the last release. The notable diff is a tiny routing header and the prefetch.window tweak. I pushed a tiny patch that strips routing-version out of cache key generation (PR 4556) — this normalizes keys across variants. Patch: ```js
function normalizeCacheKey(req) {
  const copy = {...req};
  delete copy.headers['x-routing-version'];
  return hash(copy);
}
```
cheng: Nice. If we push that as hotfix we should also revert the prefetch.window change in the rollout to be safe (set back to 50) while we validate.
morgan: Rollback/preemptive revert sounds safest for prod. We can canary the key-normalization first in EU then revert routing weight if needed.
alex: Also recommend adding a telemetry tag when cache keys are generated so future rollouts can detect key divergence quickly: emit key_hash and variant label (sampled). That would flag this automatically in the rollout gating.
sofia: Deploy plan: 1) canary PR for key-normalize to eu-canary (liz) 2) monitor kvcache.hit and main-thread parse for 10m 3) if hit_rate recovers -> promote 4) if not -> revert routing weight + prefetch.window to previous values.
liz: Pushing canary now. CI says green. Triggering canary deploy: `deploy-bot deploy canary eu-1 pr-4556` :rocket:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started deploy canary pr-4556 -> env=eu-1 id=canary-2026-03-21-eu-1
cheng: Monitoring metrics now: kvcache.hit trending up in canary, main-thread parse decreasing. Will ping in 5m with numbers.
morgan: If canary looks good we should still include the telemetry tag change as a follow-up before next routing rollout.
alex: Agreed. Also add an automated check in rollout job to compare sampled key_hash distribution across variants — fail if JS bucket differs by >5%.
sofia: Sounds good. Thx all — @liz keep us posted. If the canary stabilizes we can avoid full revert. :thumbsup:
liz: Canary shows ~28% improvement in kvcache.hit so far and LCP normalized ~+90ms -> +15ms. Pushing promote in 2m unless anyone objects.
cheng: No objections. Promoting.
sofia: Follow-up: file a small postmortem note in #postmortems with rollout diff and the gating change (alex to own).
alex: On it.
morgan: Also added a short unit test to ensure header stripping is applied before key hash (will land PR after promote).
sofia: Closing the loop here — thanks team.
